inst1:
In front of you on the screen, there will be 4 decks of cards: A, B, C, and D.

When we begin the game, I want you to select one card at a time by clicking on a card from any deck you choose.

Each time you select a card, you may win or lose some money, and it will be shown in the center of the screen. The color of the cards has nothing to do with winning or losing. The computer won't tell you in advance when you will win or lose, but you will find out as the game goes along.
inst2:
The red bar shows the money borrowed from the bank to begin the game, which is 2000 dollars. The green bar shows how much you have won. Every time you win, the green bar will increase. Every time you lose, the green bar will decrease. Once the green bar is used up, the red bar will decrease when you lose money.

You are absolutely free to switch from one deck to another at any time and as often as you wish. The goal of the game is to win as much money as possible and avoid losing as much money as possible. You won't know when the game will end. Simply keep on playing until the game stops.
inst3:
The only hint I can give you, and the most important thing to note, is this: out of these four decks of cards, some are worse than others, and to win you should try to stay away from the bad decks. No matter how much you find yourself losing, you can still win the game if you avoid the worst decks. The computer does not change the order of the cards once the game begins.

You won't know when the game will end. When the game is over, the screen will show you your final total amount.

Remember to play it like it is real money, and as if using your money.
inst4:
After the game is finished, you will be asked to complete a questionnaire related to the study.

The experiment will then be complete.

Thank you very much for your participation. Your help is greatly appreciated.
